title: External Lockout - Retries or Recycles Exceeded
shortDescription: Furnace entered lockout after too many failed ignition attempts or flame losses.
fullDescription:
Amana gas furnaces (built on Goodman platform) use an LED on the integrated control board to flash diagnostic codes. One flash indicates external lockout, typically after three failed ignition attempts or multiple flame losses during a single call for heat.

The lockout protects the heat exchanger and prevents unburned gas accumulation. Power must be cycled, or the unit will auto-reset after one hour.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass lockout. Repeated ignition failures can release unburned gas. If you smell gas, leave the home and call the utility.

causes.cause: Gas valve failure or low gas pressure

symptoms: Furnace tries to light 3 times then stops

fixSteps.title: Reset power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off furnace at switch for 60 seconds, then restore to clear lockout.

fixSteps.title: Clean flame sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove flame sensor, polish rod with fine emery cloth, reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Test igniter resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect igniter, measure 40-90 ohms cold. Replace if open or out of range.

whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC tech for gas valve or combustion issues.

faq.a: Yes, Amana boards auto-reset lockout after one hour, but the root cause remains.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
shortDescription: Pressure switch contacts are closed when they should be open (with inducer off).
fullDescription:
At the start of the heating cycle, before the inducer fan runs, the board checks that the pressure switch is open. If it reads closed, the board flashes 2 and refuses to start the inducer.

This is usually a stuck switch or miswiring. The condition is a safety check to ensure the switch can actually sense loss of draft.
safetyWarning: Never jumper a pressure switch closed - this defeats a key combustion safety and can cause CO buildup.

causes.cause: Shorted wiring between switch and board

fixSteps.title: Check switch continuity
fixSteps.instruction: With inducer off, pressure switch should read open. If closed, replace.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Look for pinched or shorted wires between switch and board harness.

whenToCallPro: If switch tests good, pro diagnosis of the board is advised.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Open
shortDescription: Inducer is running but pressure switch has not closed.
fullDescription:
After energizing the inducer, the board expects the pressure switch to close within a few seconds, proving adequate draft. Failure to close triggers 3 flashes.

Common causes are blocked venting, a clogged condensate trap (on 90%+ units), a cracked inducer wheel, or a failed switch.
safetyWarning: Blocked vents can cause flue gases including carbon monoxide to spill into the home. Verify CO alarms are working.
symptoms: Inducer runs but igniter never glows

fixSteps.title: Check PVC vents outside
fixSteps.instruction: Look for snow, ice, insect nests, or debris blocking intake/exhaust.

fixSteps.title: Clear condensate trap
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and flush the trap with warm water; clear drain line.

fixSteps.title: Check switch hose
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect rubber tubing to the pressure switch for cracks or water.

whenToCallPro: Inducer replacement and vent rework need a pro.

title: Primary Limit Switch Open
shortDescription: High-temperature limit has opened, protecting the heat exchanger.
fullDescription:
The primary limit sits in the supply plenum and opens if the furnace overheats. A 4 flash indicates it is currently open.

Overheating is usually an airflow problem: dirty filter, closed registers, blocked return, or a failing blower. Chronic tripping can crack the heat exchanger, which is a CO hazard.
safetyWarning: Repeated limit trips can damage the heat exchanger and leak carbon monoxide. Do not operate if the limit keeps opening.

causes.cause: Closed supply registers or blocked returns

symptoms: Burners light then shut off early

fixSteps.title: Replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Install a clean filter matching the required MERV rating.

fixSteps.title: Open registers and returns
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure at least 80% of registers are open and returns are unobstructed.

fixSteps.title: Check blower wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect wheel for dirt buildup; clean if heavily soiled.

whenToCallPro: If blower or heat exchanger involved, call a pro.

title: Rollout Switch Open
shortDescription: Flame rollout safety has tripped - flames escaped the burner box.
fullDescription:
Rollout switches are manual-reset thermal safeties mounted on the burner box. They trip when flames roll out, indicating a blocked heat exchanger, blocked flue, or weak inducer draft.

This is a serious safety event and requires combustion diagnosis before restoring operation.
safetyWarning: Rollout indicates flames escaped the combustion area - a fire and CO hazard. Do not reset without professional inspection.

fixSteps.title: Call pro immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Do not reset. Schedule combustion analysis and heat exchanger inspection.

whenToCallPro: Always. This is a combustion safety - pro only.

faq.q: Can I just reset the button?
faq.a: No. Resetting without finding the cause risks fire and CO poisoning.

title: 115 VAC Polarity Reversed
shortDescription: Line and neutral wires are reversed on the furnace power supply.
fullDescription:
Amana control boards detect hot/neutral polarity. If reversed, the flame-sensing circuit cannot function because flame rectification depends on a proper ground reference.

The board flashes 6 and disables ignition until corrected.
safetyWarning: Reversed polarity is an electrical hazard. Disconnect power before working on wiring.

causes.cause: Loose neutral at furnace junction box

fixSteps.title: Test outlet/disconnect polarity
fixSteps.instruction: Use outlet tester or multimeter to verify L1 is hot, neutral bonded.

fixSteps.title: Correct wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Swap wires if reversed. Licensed electrician recommended.

title: Gas Valve Circuit Error
shortDescription: Board detects a problem energizing the gas valve.
fullDescription:
A 7 flash indicates the gas valve relay on the board is not responding correctly - either the valve coil is open, shorted, or wiring is interrupted.

Ignition will not proceed. This requires pro diagnosis because gas components are involved.
safetyWarning: Do not attempt gas valve work without proper training and leak-testing equipment.

fixSteps.title: Call HVAC pro
fixSteps.instruction: Gas valve diagnosis requires manometer and leak detection.

title: Low Flame Signal
shortDescription: Flame is lit but sense current is below the weak threshold.
fullDescription:
The flame sensor rectifies a tiny AC current through the flame to DC. Amana boards need roughly 0.5-1.0 microamps to confirm flame. Below that, the 8 flash warns of marginal sensing.

Commonly caused by a dirty sensor, weak flame, or poor ground.
safetyWarning: Chronic low flame can lead to lockouts and unburned gas cycling.

causes.cause: Poor burner flame (low gas pressure, dirty burners)

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Polish with emery cloth, reinstall, and test.

fixSteps.title: Measure microamps
fixSteps.instruction: Meter in series on sensor wire should read 1-5 microamps steady.

whenToCallPro: If sensor clean does not fix, pro diagnosis needed.

title: High Stage Pressure Switch Fault
shortDescription: High-fire pressure switch failed to close during two-stage operation.
fullDescription:
Two-stage Amana furnaces have separate pressure switches for low and high fire. The 9 flash means the high-stage switch did not close when commanded, usually due to a weak inducer on high speed, partial vent obstruction, or a failed switch.

The furnace drops back to low fire and notifies via the LED.
safetyWarning: A partially obstructed vent can produce CO. Verify detectors.

fixSteps.title: Inspect vent
fixSteps.instruction: Verify no partial obstructions; measure static pressure.

title: Low 24V Voltage
shortDescription: Secondary transformer voltage below minimum operating range.
fullDescription:
The 24VAC control circuit voltage is below about 18V, suggesting a weak transformer, overloaded secondary, or shorted low-voltage accessory (e.g., humidifier, zone panel).

The board halts operation to protect components.
safetyWarning: Short in low-voltage wiring can heat wires and damage transformer.

fixSteps.title: Measure 24V at R/C
fixSteps.instruction: Should read 22-28V. If low, disconnect accessories one by one.
